# Code style

- STY-005: Nullable reference types are on in every project and stay on in every file: no #nullable directive, no null-forgiving operator (!, null!, default!) outside a test project (a name ending in Tests) without the comment // CRF-001 safety net: <reason> on its line or the line above, and no file marked as generated code (a generated name or an <auto-generated> comment) that a tool didn't write into source; EF Core's migrations, in a Migrations folder, may carry the marker and #nullable disable, and a .resx file's designer the marker.
- STY-008: Every publicly visible type and member has an XML documentation comment; STY-015 leaves test projects out.
- STY-013: Choose Nullable enable for new projects and active projects where you want to protect against null reference exceptions. A project that migrated to nullable reference types ends with <Nullable>enable</Nullable> and no #nullable directives. Use the null-forgiving operator sparingly: prefer a null check, restructuring the code, or annotating the relevant API so the compiler reaches the right conclusion on its own.
- STY-015: Test projects (names ending in Tests) and the project BenchmarkDotNet generates for a run are left out of STY-008's XML documentation requirement.
